title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements Between Systems
objective: I can use ratio reasoning to convert measurements between the customary and metric systems.
model: ratio table / double number line built from one approximate conversion factor (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb), with a size check on the direction

widgets.component: within-system conversion warm-up (cups/quarts, m/cm, ft/in, L/mL)
widgets.root: Matches the lesson's own warm-up (config warmup.questions) and the earlier 3-6 skill it builds on; keys checked (12 cups, 2.4 m, 12 in/1 ft, 5,000 mL).

widgets.component: between-system word problems with the factor given (km to mi, lb to kg, L to qt, cups to L)
widgets.root: Mathematics recomputed for every key (3 mi, 4.5 kg, 48 mi, 10-25 kg package, 4.24 qt, 10 kg, 3.6 L). The factor is stated, so the reasoning is direction and scaling, not recall.

widgets.component: ratio-table fill-ins (km to mi with 1 : 0.6 row; lb to kg with 1 : 0.45 row)
widgets.root: Real ratio tables with the factor row shown and later rows scaled by 10, 30, 40; matches the lesson's representation. Not manipulable, but a manipulable chain exists in §4.7.

widgets.component: tap-the-first-wrong-step: divides instead of multiplying (20 ÷ 0.6), and writes = after a rounded factor
widgets.root: The two real misconceptions of this lesson (direction of the operation, ≈ versus =); e indexes checked against the step arrays.

widgets.component: double number line with the unit ladder 0, 1, 2 … and one blank
widgets.root: Parametric inline SVG; 300 seeds rendered, zero tick aligned with zero on both lines and the bottom row is exactly factor × top row. The ladder lets a student skip-count to the blank, which is weak but is the L1 scaffold.

widgets.component: generated cm to in, L to qt word problems, 'round to the nearest tenth'
widgets.root: Generator answers independently checked by the repo test (300 seeds x 4 levels); stems state the factor and the rounding place.

widgets.component: conversion chain: choose multiply or divide and a factor tile, running number and unit update
widgets.root: Manipulable model of the lesson's idea. A miss explains the direction logic ('kilometers are the longer unit, so fewer miles') without the number; the rounding place is a separate step. It is a chain, not a ratio table, but it exercises the same scaling.

widgets.component: mastery check: scale 10 km, 30 lb, why ≈, 100 km/h versus 100 mi/h
widgets.root: Matches the worked example (the Canadian highway sign) and the reasonableness vocabulary; keys correct (6 mi, 13.5 kg, 'rounded approximations', slower).

widgets.component: ladder of generated conversions ending in a 'which is greater' comparison
widgets.root: L4 compares 13 qt with 10 L after converting; keys recomputed across seeds.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 (err, wr, tbl, mc, num, mc, tbl)
widgets.component: multi-step missions: equal numbers in different units, bridge-weight cars, airline limit, coolant bottles, mi/h speed, inventory sheet
widgets.root: All keys recomputed (10,715 cars, 41.8 lb over 40 by 1.8, 22 bottles, 2 mi/h over). Num items carry feedback for each wrong path (subtracting across units, dividing the wrong way).

widgets.component: longer chains with rounding, and a reasonable / not reasonable sort of six claims
widgets.root: Sort cards verified (10 km ≈ 6 mi yes, 4 kg ≈ 1.8 lb no, 20 in ≈ 51 cm yes, 3 L ≈ 0.3 qt no, 100 lb ≈ 45 kg yes, 5 mi ≈ 3 km no); the sort trains the direction check that the lesson names 'reasonableness'.

widgets.component: bug-detective steps, exact versus rounded factor (= only for 1 in = 2.54 cm), comparison of 5 mi and 8 km, tank, arm limit, write-your-own
widgets.root: Mathematics correct; 5.2 and 5.3 correctly teach that only 2.54 is exact and that 5 mi ≈ 8 km.
